newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish debt yields end higher on EMU worries.
newsitem.headline: Swedish debt yields end higher on EMU worries.

text.p: The Swedish crown weakened and debt yields rose on Monday in the wake of uncertainites surounding the Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU).
The major question unsettling the market was whether there would be a snap general election in France, nine months ahead of schedule.
However traders said the result of the election was not that worrying.
"But it would be good to know what will happens. Initially it might not be positive, but in the long run it should be," one dealer said.
Six-month T-bill rates rose three basis points to 4.16 percent. The ten-year bond yields broke resistence level at 7.24 percent to close nine basis points higher at 7.25 percent.

A statement by the Swedish Centre Party leader, Olof Johansson, saying if the minority Social Democratic government gave EMU the nod, it could end cooperation between the two parties had no major impact, dealers said.

The crown softened to 4.4875 to the mark from 4.4645 late on Friday. "As soon as the crown aproaches 4.49 against the mark buyers are attracted into the market", one dealer said. -- Barbara Taltavull, Stockholm newsroom +46-8-700 1019
